claims.text: Successful formation of noble metal–based high-entropy alloy nanoparticles is governed by optimization of surface energy.
Successful formation of noble metal–based high-entropy alloy nanoparticles is governed by atomic interactions among the constituent elements.
Changing elemental composition and ratios can optimize surface energy and atomic interactions.
Optimized surface energy and atomic interactions lead to homogeneous alloy formation.
Optimized surface energy and atomic interactions preserve substantial surface-atom exposure.
The optimized nanoparticles will exhibit better catalytic performance than the unoptimized baseline.
The optimized nanoparticles will exhibit better stability than the unoptimized baseline.
The hypothesis applies to noble metal–based high-entropy alloy nanoparticles containing more than five interacting elements.
The hypothesis does not apply to systems containing fewer elements.
The hypothesis does not apply to non-noble-metal systems.
The exact relationship among surface energy, atomic interactions, and alloy formation is not well understood.
The proposed comparison contrasts nanoparticles assigned optimized elemental compositions and ratios with an unoptimized baseline.
